title: Upwards and Onwards
summary:
Changing Chinese import patterns scramble tanker trades
In the decade prior to Covid, Chinese crude oil imports were growing rapidly, from 4.1 million barrels per day (Mb/d) in 2009 to 10.1 Mb/d in 2019, an average annual growth rate of 9.5%. Mainly as a result of the Covid pandemic, Chinese crude oil demand growth slowed to a crawl in recent years, with 2021 actually registering a 550,000 b/d decline. So far in 2022, Chinese imports have been quite volatile as temporary Covid lockdowns in major cities dampened oil demand and stunted the recovery.
